biggest_catch: Most contributors do 5–20 hours a week and higher rates require real domain expertise - the open all-access tier pays less per task.
catches: Not a job: project-based, no employment contract, no fixed hours, no guaranteed income.
You earn per completed, ACCEPTED task - rejected tasks are unpaid.
Specialized projects require domain expertise (70% of contributors hold a Master's or PhD).
All-access tasks are open to everyone but 'offer lower pay for quicker, less demanding tasks'.
Work is subject to project availability - contributors mostly participate alongside a primary career.

c2.evidence: Mindrift.ai official FAQ: 'Payments are processed bi-weekly. You earn per completed, accepted task and the amount is shown before you start.'

c3.evidence: Free to apply; no upfront fee documented.

eligibility: Apply with a CV; pass project qualification; domain expertise required for specialized projects; all-access tasks open to everyone.
maximize: Mindrift is repeatable and officially documented: its FAQ states specialized projects pay $15–$100+/hour with bi-weekly payments. Apply with a CV that proves real domain expertise - Mindrift says 70% of contributors hold a Master's or PhD - since that tier pays the premium rates. Compensation is always visible before you begin each task, so only accept tasks whose stated pay justifies your time.
